text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Gynecologic oncology consultation in two weeks for a friable cervical mass with bleeding and pain, biopsied today: diagnosis, staging, treatment intent, bleeding control, and pain
  • Stop opium tincture and change to measured oral morphine solution 5 mg every 4 hours as needed with an oral syringe, with acetaminophen, senna and polyethylene glycol, a naloxone nasal spray, a prescription monitoring check, locked storage, one prescriber, and review in two weeks
  • Iron deficiency anemia: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg intravenously today and in two weeks, with a blood count at each visit and ferritin 6 to 8 weeks after the infusions
  • Blood tests: blood count, ferritin, creatinine, ALT, albumin and a pregnancy test; HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests before any cancer treatment; PHQ-9
  • Staging by FIGO 1843 with pelvic MRI and PET-CT, and a CT-guided biopsy of a lung nodule; tumor PD-L1, mismatch repair and HER2 testing; no germline testing, because cervical cancer is not a hereditary cancer syndrome
  • Palliative pelvic radiation, 20 Gy in 5 fractions, for bleeding and pain, then carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab every 3 weeks for six cycles with pembrolizumab continuing, without bevacizumab while bleeding and after pelvic radiation; blood counts before each cycle and thyroid tests every six weeks
  • Specialist palliative care alongside cancer treatment from diagnosis, for pain, symptoms, mood, and goals-of-care conversations, with long-acting morphine 15 mg every 12 hours and oral morphine 5 mg as needed for breakthrough pain

resource.title: Ada Lovelace synthetic care plan
resource.description: Primary care, gynecologic oncology and early palliative care for a 35-year-old mathematician with five months of abnormal bleeding and pelvic pain who has taken prescribed opium tincture for years: speculum examination and biopsy of a visible cervical tumor at the first visit, with tumor HPV typing; intravenous iron for iron deficiency anemia from blood loss; conversion of an unmeasured opium tincture to measured oral morphine, then long-acting morphine, with naloxone, a bowel regimen, safe storage and a prescription monitoring check, applying the ASCO 1848 guideline on opioids for cancer pain and noting that the CDC 1847 opioid guideline does not cover cancer pain; FIGO 1843 staging with MRI and PET-CT and biopsy of a lung metastasis (stage IVB); tumor biomarkers (PD-L1, mismatch repair, HER2) and why germline testing is not indicated; palliative pelvic radiation for bleeding; first-line carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab under the NCCN cervical cancer guideline and KEYNOTE-826, without bevacizumab while she was bleeding after pelvic radiation; specialist palliative care from diagnosis (ASCO 1849); immune-related thyroid monitoring; opioid-induced constipation; goals-of-care conversations and advance care planning; vaccination of an adult on chemotherapy; and protecting clear-headed hours for her mathematical work.

code.text: Gynecologic oncology consultation in two weeks for a friable cervical mass with bleeding and pain, biopsied today: diagnosis, staging, treatment intent, bleeding control, and pain

Stop opium tincture and change to measured oral morphine solution 5 mg every 4 hours as needed with an oral syringe, with acetaminophen, senna and polyethylene glycol, a naloxone nasal spray, a prescription monitoring check, locked storage, one prescriber, and review in two weeks
Iron deficiency anemia: ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg intravenously today and in two weeks, with a blood count at each visit and ferritin 6 to 8 weeks after the infusions
Blood tests: blood count, ferritin, creatinine, ALT, albumin and a pregnancy test; HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests before any cancer treatment; PHQ-9

Staging by FIGO 1843 with pelvic MRI and PET-CT, and a CT-guided biopsy of a lung nodule; tumor PD-L1, mismatch repair and HER2 testing; no germline testing, because cervical cancer is not a hereditary cancer syndrome

Palliative pelvic radiation, 20 Gy in 5 fractions, for bleeding and pain, then carboplatin, paclitaxel and pembrolizumab every 3 weeks for six cycles with pembrolizumab continuing, without bevacizumab while bleeding and after pelvic radiation; blood counts before each cycle and thyroid tests every six weeks

Specialist palliative care alongside cancer treatment from diagnosis, for pain, symptoms, mood, and goals-of-care conversations, with long-acting morphine 15 mg every 12 hours and oral morphine 5 mg as needed for breakthrough pain
Referral to gynecologic oncology
